# Independent audit: the global intrinsic lift of thin-fiber laws

**Result: PASS.** This is a line-by-line independent audit of
`candidate 4103337048e3d0cb`, including
its compactness, measure, incidence, and lattice-reduction assertions.
The exact verifier `supporting computation verify_global_intrinsic_thin_lift.py` passes under
`work/math-venv/bin/python`.
The companion checks `supporting computation verify_normalized_thin_ball_lifts.py` and
`supporting computation verify_vanishing_coarse_mass_obstructions.py` were also rerun and pass.

The original density argument correctly identified a classical Borell
characterization as its imported input. For the bounded actual-body
hypotheses here that input has now been removed entirely. Section 2
below records the elementary replacement from the already proved
companion construction; with the author's agreement it was inserted
directly into the theorem note and independently checked there. No
geometric or measure-theoretic counterexample to the theorem was found.

## 1. Positive mass and exact support

The common bounded support and finite number of bases ensure that
weak convergence preserves every fiber's total mass and that sum p_z=1.
For p_z>0 the prelimit fibers have positive full m-volume eventually,
so their conditional uniform probabilities are well-defined and
converge to mu_z/p_z.

The support proof has the correct Portmanteau direction. For every
limiting support candidate x, a homothetic copy of the ENTIRE prelimit
body about a nearby x_l has relative volume t^m and lies in the stated
closed ball for all sufficiently large l. Upper Portmanteau bounds
the limsup by the limit's mass of that closed ball, giving a positive
lower bound for the latter. Applying the statement to a smaller
closed ball inside any given open neighborhood proves genuine support
membership, not merely positive mass of one closed neighborhood.
Hausdorff convergence excludes support outside K_z. This includes
exposed points, points on collapsed facets, and supports of dimension
zero. Volume continuity then correctly yields q_z<m when M_l tends
to zero.

## 2. An elementary density construction in precisely these hypotheses

Here is a self-contained replacement for importing the concave-measure
classification. Fix one surviving fiber with q>0 and r=m-q. Project
orthogonally onto E=aff K_z, and use a fixed isometric identification
of its direction with R^q. Projection of K_(z,l) converges to K_z,
so it contains a fixed q-ball for all large l. Form the simultaneous
ball replacement of the companion note, but for this SINGLE fiber,
using the normalizer 1/M_l:

    A_l={(xi,y): xi in projection K_(z,l),
        |y| <= [vol_r(K_(z,l) at xi)/(M_l kappa_r)]^(1/r)}.

Brunn--Minkowski in the perpendicular r-sections proves convexity and
concavity of its radius. Compact original sections give upper
semicontinuity, so A_l is closed. Its m-volume is p_(z,l)<=1 and its
projected volume law is exactly the projected normalized source law.

If its largest radius is H_l and the common projection inball has
radius rho, convexity gives hidden radius at least H_l/2 on a
q-ball of radius rho/2. Therefore

    1 >= kappa_r(H_l/2)^r kappa_q(rho/2)^q.

Both projections and radii are uniformly bounded. Blaschke selection
gives a compact convex subsequential limit A. Its m-volume is p_z>0
by volume continuity, so A has full dimension m. Its volume measures
converge in L1, and their projections are exactly mu_z. Rotational
symmetry of the hidden sections passes to A; its sections are centered
r-balls with a bounded upper semicontinuous concave radius R(xi).
Thus mu_z has density f_z=kappa_r R^r, giving the asserted exponent
1/r, positive continuity on the relative interior, and the canonical
closed boundary representative.

This is the single-fiber specialization of Section 5 of
`candidate b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e`, whose
radius bound, positive-volume limit, and projection identities were
checked directly in this audit. It does not use the GLOBAL lift being
proved and does not assume the different source directions align.
For q=0 the support statement already makes mu_z a point mass; the
radius-(p_z/kappa_m)^(1/m) ball supplies its explicit lift.

The original alternative classification uses the correct conversion
from measure exponent 1/m to density exponent 1/(m-q). It is a
classical input, rather than a theorem proved from scratch in the
companion; the parameter statement is recorded in the cited
[Fradelizi--Guedon paper](https://perso.math.u-pem.fr/guedon.olivier/Articles/02/Fradelizi-Guedon.pdf).
The elementary construction above makes it unnecessary for the present
bounded thin-body result.

## 3. Arbitrary integer incidence, including the target

Equation (2) follows from ordinary finite Brunn--Minkowski after
division by the SAME total mass M_l, before taking limits. It implies
both positivity of every integer target and lattice-convexity of P_+.
It is valid for arbitrary finite anchored combinations, not just
midpoints or a chosen generating family of relations.

For each positive source, fixing points in the other sources proves
the translated containment lambda K_source+t_l subset K_target.
The target/source volume ratio is bounded because the source has a
fixed positive share of M_l and the target is one of the fibers summed
in M_l. The displayed cone proof of width comparability is correct:
after normalization the target contains a radius-lambda ball, and
the cone from its perpendicular (m-1)-disk to any target point has
the claimed volume. The m=1 case uses the one-point H_0 base and
gives its segment length. Taking difference-body support functions
does not lose a factor two: both bodies' minimum comparison balls
are doubled when difference bodies are formed.

Passing those two-sided width bounds to the Hausdorff limits gives
EXACT equality of every source and target direction space in the
representation. The affine hull of a positive-weight Minkowski sum
of full relative q-dimensional sets with parallel directions is the
sum of their affine hulls. Its inclusion in the target q-plane proves
the offset identity modulo U. This includes q=0. No global affine
offset alignment is used.

## 4. Cross-measure inequality and the optimized radii

The weak-limit cross-measure inequality is valid for compact positive-
mass source sets. Their open epsilon neighborhoods and the closed
2epsilon neighborhood of their compact Minkowski average have the
required containment. Lower Portmanteau on the sources and upper
Portmanteau on the target yield the stated direction. Decreasing
epsilon then uses continuity from above of finite measures. Ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski may be applied to compact subsets approaching the
source neighborhood masses, so no measurability of an arbitrary
noncompact Minkowski sum is required.

For q>0, interior source points average to an interior point of the
target in the common affine q-plane: their small q-balls already
have a q-ball as their Minkowski average inside that target. The
small-ball limit cancels the same kappa_q and epsilon^(q/m) factors
on both sides. The optimization over radii is indispensable and
correct: weighted Holder, or the stated concave-power Jensen argument,
gives its maximum S^((m-q)/m), attained at a_i=b_i/S. All b_i are
positive at the selected interior points. The resulting root-density
inequality has exponent 1/(m-q), exactly as required for the hidden
ball radii. At q=0 singleton test sets give the ball-volume root
inequality directly, with no density differentiation.

## 5. One hidden space and exact intrinsic measure

At every fiber U_z in the original x-space is orthogonal to the
chosen hidden V_(m-q_z) in the ADDED y-space. Their Euclidean product
measure is therefore exactly H_m with Jacobian one. Integrating the
hidden ball volumes gives p_z and the ENTIRE original finite law mu_z,
including the point-mass case. The positive relative interior proves
dimension exactly m in each case.

Every actual integer representation has a common q and hence a common
hidden subspace V_(m-q). Triangle inequality plus the optimized root
inequality proves its lift inclusion. Unrelated fibers may have
different directions or dimensions; this causes no missing case,
because an integer representation mixing them would already violate
the incidence theorem. Approximation by relative interior points
extends the inclusion to all closed boundary points, including
nonzero boundary density traces.

The hull proof correctly combines repeated source bases, discards only
zero coefficients, and invokes an arbitrary anchored inclusion. It
therefore obtains EXACT integer fibers rather than merely one-sided
containment. Lattice-convexity of P_+ excludes all additional integer
bases.

## 6. Relative lattice reduction and the dimension bound

The direction F=span(P_+-z0) is rational. Its lattice F intersect Z^k
is saturated: if an integer multiple of an integer vector belongs
to F, the vector already belongs to F. A basis of this primitive
sublattice extends to a unimodular basis. The stated base translation,
change of coordinates, and deletion thus identify the affine lattice
EXACTLY with Z^(k'); they do not create new bases.

In the affine hull G of the lifted body, the vertical kernel W is a
subspace of the 2m-dimensional continuous space. It contains each
m-dimensional fiber direction, so m<=D=dim W<=2m. Projection of G
onto the reduced base is surjective, giving an affine section b and
the displayed description of G. An isometry W->R^D, after subtracting
b(z), is an affine bijection from G to R^(k') times R^D. The hull is
full dimensional relative to G, so its image is an actual full-
dimensional convex body.

At a FIXED base the map is a translation followed by an isometry on
every m-plane. It preserves H_m exactly even when the original fiber
directions differ. No ambient determinant or base-shear determinant
is being used as an intrinsic fiber Jacobian. The reduced mixed set
has maximum fiber dimension m, even if D>m; the note states this
distinction correctly.

## 7. Projection of closed caps and the final scope

The inverse relative map, original-x projection, and inverse base
embedding compose to one affine map. The exact pushforward measure
identity follows fiber by fiber. Pulling back an original closed cap
gives a closed halfspace or a constant condition; if it contains the
projected point the latter condition includes the whole source.
Consequently depth transfers in the stated direction for every lifted
mixed point. Such a point projects into its actual limiting support
fiber, by the exact integer-fiber and support identities already
proved.

The two-triangle calibration checks: each limiting density is
(t+1)/4, its hidden interval radius is (t+1)/8, and its intrinsic
triangle area is 1/2. Extreme-base isolation and the ordinary triangle
cap bound give lifted maximum 2/9. The projected law has maximum 1/4.
Thus the note correctly denies equality under projection and any
automatic prelimit depth or fine-lattice recovery.

The newly required dependencies have direct proofs in the audited
files: support/hull continuity, width comparability, the elementary
ball compactness construction, and the optimized cross-density
inequality. Standard Brunn--Minkowski, Blaschke selection, volume
continuity, and saturated-lattice linear algebra remain ordinary
background. No mixed OC theorem or missing sharp allocation lemma
is used.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
